editorialNotice: Stories are Akhlaq's brief summaries of the cited Quran passages, not Quran quotations or a new tafsir. Practice ideas are practical applications, not additional prescribed rituals, counts or promised rewards.

practices.title: Read a little Quran
practices.cue: After a prayer you already observe
practices.action: Read a short passage and its translation. Choose an amount you can manage, and return to the same place in your day.

practices.title: Pause before speaking
practices.action: Check whether your words are truthful, useful and considerate. If a reply would only hurt someone, pause before sending it.

practices.title: Do a small act of kindness
practices.action: Offer practical help, make a task easier, or give what you can. The suggestion is an everyday application of the hadith, not a fixed daily obligation.

practices.title: Make time for your parents
practices.cue: At a suitable time in your week
practices.action: If possible and safe, ask how a parent is doing or help with something they need. Adapt the action to your circumstances.

practices.title: Practise self-control
practices.action: Pause before reacting and choose words or actions that do not harm. Consider what a calm response would look like.

practices.title: Be honest in a small moment
practices.cue: When giving an answer or making a promise
practices.action: Avoid exaggerating or saying what you do not know. Correct an inaccurate statement when you notice it.

practices.title: Remember Allah
practices.cue: At a quiet moment in your day
practices.action: Read the two phrases in the linked hadith and remember Allah. This suggestion does not assign a prescribed repetition count or a special time.

practices.title: Bring attention to your meal
practices.action: Read the Prophet's advice to Umar ibn Abi Salamah about mentioning Allah's name, using the right hand and eating from what is near.

practices.title: Want good for someone else
practices.cue: When you hear another person's news
practices.action: Consider the good you would wish for yourself and wish it for your brother too. Look for a sincere, helpful way to respond.

stories.name: Adam
stories.title: Returning to Allah

parts.text: Adam and his wife were permitted to live in the Garden and eat freely, with a warning not to approach a particular tree. After Satan caused them to slip, they were sent down to earth. Adam then received words from his Lord, and Allah accepted his repentance.

stories.reflection: When you make a mistake, what would a sincere next step look like?

stories.name: Nuh · Noah
stories.title: Continuing through ridicule

parts.text: Allah instructed Nuh to build the Ark. As he worked, leaders from his people mocked him. When the command came, he took aboard those he had been instructed to take, and the Ark sailed through immense waves.
Nuh called to his son to join them, but his son trusted that a mountain would protect him and was drowned. The passage then describes the water receding and the Ark coming to rest on Mount Judi.

stories.reflection: What worthwhile responsibility can you continue with patience, even when others do not understand?

stories.name: Ibrahim · Abraham
stories.title: Faith in the face of opposition

parts.text: Ibrahim broke the idols except the largest. When questioned, he challenged his people to consider whether their idols could speak or bring benefit or harm. They called for him to be burned. Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim.

stories.reflection: What do these verses invite you to think about concerning worship and trust in Allah?

stories.name: Yusuf · Joseph
stories.title: Choosing forgiveness

parts.text: Yusuf's brothers recognised him and admitted that they had done wrong. Yusuf spoke of Allah's favour, patience and mindfulness of Allah. He then told them that they would face no reproach from him that day and prayed for Allah to forgive them.

stories.reflection: Is there a safe, appropriate step towards forgiveness you want to reflect on?

stories.name: Musa · Moses
stories.title: Guidance when the way seems closed

parts.text: Allah showed Musa signs involving his staff and his hand, and instructed him to go to Pharaoh, who had transgressed.

Later, when Musa's companions feared they were about to be overtaken, Musa expressed trust in his Lord's guidance. Allah instructed him to strike the sea with his staff. The sea parted, and Musa and all those with him were saved.

stories.reflection: How might trust in Allah and taking the next responsible action sit together?

stories.name: Yunus · Jonah
stories.title: Calling out from distress

parts.text: The Quran recalls Yunus, the Man of the Whale, leaving in anger and then calling to Allah from darkness. He declared Allah's oneness and acknowledged his own wrongdoing. Allah answered him and rescued him from distress.

stories.reflection: What would you like to bring honestly to Allah in your own supplication?

stories.name: Ayyub · Job
stories.title: Turning to Allah in hardship

parts.text: Ayyub called upon his Lord about the adversity that had touched him and appealed to Allah's mercy. Allah answered him, removed his hardship and restored his family, with as many again. The passage describes this as a mercy and a reminder for worshippers.

stories.reflection: What support and supplication could help you meet a difficult day?

stories.name: Isa · Jesus
stories.title: Worship and care for his mother

parts.text: In Surah Maryam, Isa identifies himself as Allah's servant and a prophet. He speaks of the Scripture, prayer, zakah and dutifulness to his mother. The passage affirms worship of Allah as the straight path.

stories.reflection: How can worship and care for your family both have a place in your day?
